page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine configuration built on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at a 3.7 GHz clock speed and supports AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, and virtualization extensions. System memory is sized at 512.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. The platform incorporates 15,359 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage and contains no discrete graphics processors.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent computational and I/O efficiency across multi-threaded scenarios. The configuration achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,342.0, placing it within the top decile of evaluated systems, alongside a single-core score of 2,082.0. Multithreaded compression and decompression workloads reflect this processing capacity, registering 366.38 GB/sec in parallel bzip3 decompression. In-memory data store performance is underscored by 89.18 million operations per second during Redis SET testing, while PassMark database operations record 27,733.64 points.

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate 4,861.79 GB/sec in cached small-block reads, tapering to 150.96 GB/sec during large-block uncached read operations and 106.62 GB/sec on sequential writes. Small-model LLM prompt processing delivers 3,999.55 tokens per second for 135M parameter models, although throughput scales down to 16.65 tokens per second for larger 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration.

The dense pairing of 15,359 GB NVMe storage and 512 GB of RAM delivers high cost efficiency for storage-bound applications by avoiding the added operational costs and latency penalties of network-attached block devices. Primary workload fits include high-throughput relational databases, distributed NoSQL clusters, transactional indexing engines, large-scale data warehousing, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, it supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 512.0 GB of system memory, and 15,359 GB of bundled NVMe SSD local storage without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in the upper tiers of multi-threaded execution, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,342.0, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speeds of 366.38 GB/sec, and 89.18 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 4,861.79 GB/sec for cached transfers and 106.62 GB/sec for uncached write operations. The high ratio of local NVMe storage to compute resources renders the instance technically suitable for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data processing, and large-scale analytical storage systems.
